method_card.title: Food, Drink and Meals
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, expressing preferences with adverbs of manner, ordering politely and talking about mealtimes.

GermanEnglish
das Brotbread
der Käsecheese
das Fleischmeat
der Fischfish
das Hähnchenchicken
das Obstfruit
das Gemüsevegetables
die Nudeln (pl.)pasta / noodles
der Reisrice
die Milchmilk
der Orangensaftorange juice
gernlike (doing)
lieberprefer (doing)
am liebstenlike most (doing)
ich möchte / ich hätte gernI would like
zum Frühstück / Mittagessen / Abendessenfor breakfast / lunch / dinner

Grammar focus — gern / lieber / am liebsten: In German, to say you like doing something, you use the verb + gern (not a separate verb like mögen). Ich esse gern Obst. (I like eating fruit.) Ich esse lieber Hähnchen. (I prefer eating chicken.) Am liebsten esse ich Pizza. (I like eating pizza most of all — note: am liebsten often fronts the sentence.) These adverbs always come after the verb, never before.

The strong verb essen (to eat) has a stem-vowel change in the 2nd and 3rd person singular: du isst, er/sie isst (note: no 'e' in the middle — isst, not esst).

Model: Zum Frühstück esse ich Brot mit Käse und trinke Orangensaft. Ich esse lieber Fisch als Fleisch, weil er gesünder ist. Am liebsten esse ich Nudeln. (For breakfast I eat bread with cheese and drink orange juice. I prefer eating fish to meat, because it is healthier. I like eating pasta most of all.)
steps: Learn food and drink nouns with their genders (der/die/das) — every noun needs its article
Use gern / lieber / am liebsten AFTER the verb to express preferences
Order food politely with ich möchte or ich hätte gern (formal Sie register in restaurants)
Describe meals using zum Frühstück / Mittagessen / Abendessen + verb at position 2

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — food appears in restaurant role plays and writing tasks

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Ich esse lieber Fisch, weil er frisch und gesund ist.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich esse lieber Fisch: esse = eat (ich form), lieber = prefer (comes after the verb), Fisch = fish.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: weil = because. After weil, the verb goes to the END: er frisch und gesund ist (it is fresh and healthy).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I prefer eating fish because it is fresh and healthy.

worked_examples.question: How do you order food politely in a café using 'ich hätte gern'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich hätte gern = I would like — this is Konjunktiv II (conditional), making the request polite. Always use this in café / restaurant / shop role plays.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Add the food item in the accusative after gern. For a specific drink, say ein Glas + drink: Ich hätte gern ein Glas Orangensaft.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich hätte gern einmal Schnitzel und ein Glas Wasser, bitte. (I would like one schnitzel and a glass of water, please.)

bronze.question: Match the German food words to the English meaning
Match the German drink words and food adjectives to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct adverb of preference

gaps.correct_explain: gern (like doing) comes after the verb esse: Ich esse gern Obst. Note: German uses verb + gern, not a separate verb like English 'like'.

wrong.lieber: lieber means 'prefer' (comparison). For simply liking something, use gern.
wrong.mag: mag (like) uses a different structure: Ich mag Obst. The question asks for the adverb-of-manner structure with essen, so use gern.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence about mealtimes
sentence_parts: esse ich Brot mit Käse und trinke Orangensaft.

gaps.correct_explain: Zum Frühstück = for breakfast. Zum (= zu + dem, dative) + meal name is the standard German pattern.

wrong.Abendessen: Zum Abendessen means 'for dinner / in the evening'. Bread and cheese with orange juice is more typical of breakfast.
wrong.Mittagessen: Zum Mittagessen means 'for lunch'. A hot meal is more typical for lunch in Germany.

bronze.question: What does 'Mein Bruder isst nicht gern Gemüse' mean?
options: My brother doesn't like eating vegetables
My brother eats vegetables every day
My brother prefers vegetables to fruit

bronze.question: What does 'Ich hätte gern ein Glas Wasser, bitte' mean?
options: I would like a glass of water, please
I have a glass of water, please
I had a glass of water

bronze.source_text: Zum Frühstück trinke ich Orangensaft und esse Brot.
model_answers: For breakfast I drink orange juice and eat bread.
hints: trinke = I drink (fronted phrase → verb at position 2, subject after)

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: My brother doesn't **like eating** vegetables because he **finds** them disgusting.
sentence_parts: nicht gern Gemüse, weil er es ekelhaft

gaps.rule: Strong verb — essen (er/sie/es form, stem-vowel change)
gaps.correct_explain: isst is the er/sie/es form of essen. Note the stem-vowel change: essen → er isst (e → i).

wrong.esse: esse is the ich form. The subject is Bruder (he), so use isst.
wrong.esst: esst is the ihr form (you plural). For Bruder (he), use isst.

gaps.correct_explain: After weil, the conjugated verb goes to the END: weil er es ekelhaft findet.

wrong.finden: finden is the infinitive or wir/sie form. In a weil clause, you still need the conjugated er/sie form: findet.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.explanation: Cola is a drink, so use trinke (drink), not esse (eat): Ich trinke gern Cola.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: For lunch I eat chicken because it is tasty.

distractor_labels.isst: wrong conjugation — isst is the du/er/sie form. The subject is ich: esse

silver.source_text: I would like one fish and chips and a glass of water, please.
model_answers: Ich möchte einmal Fisch und Pommes und ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
Ich hätte gern einmal Fisch und Pommes und ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
hints: fish and chips = Fisch und Pommes
a glass of water = ein Glas Wasser

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: For breakfast I eat bread with cheese and drink orange juice. I prefer eating chicken because it contains a lot of protein. Yesterday I ate pasta and it was very tasty.
model_answers: Zum Frühstück esse ich Brot mit Käse und trinke Orangensaft. Ich esse lieber Hähnchen, weil es viel Protein enthält. Gestern habe ich Nudeln gegessen und es war sehr lecker.

Check: zum + meal (dative), gern/lieber after verb, weil + verb at end, perfect tense habe gegessen (weak participle ge-ess-en, or gegessen — irregular strong), three time frames (present, reason clause, past). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: Yesterday I ate cake and drank coffee.

distractor_labels.esse: wrong tense — esse is present tense. Gestern (yesterday) requires the perfect tense: habe gegessen
distractor_labels.trinke: wrong tense — trinke is present tense. Use the perfect tense past participle: getrunken

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are on holiday in Germany and visit a restaurant for dinner with your family. The waiter comes to your table.

bullets.prompt: Greet the waiter and ask if there is a table for three people.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Abend! Haben Sie einen Tisch für drei Personen, bitte?
bullets.note: Sie register — formal restaurant context; Haben Sie...? (polite question); einen Tisch (accusative masculine)

bullets.prompt: Order food and a drink for yourself.
bullets.model_answer: Ich hätte gern einmal Hähnchen mit Nudeln und ein Glas Orangensaft, bitte.
bullets.note: ich hätte gern (polite Konjunktiv II); einmal for food portions; ein Glas + drink

bullets.prompt: Say what you thought of the food (past tense and opinion).
bullets.model_answer: Ich habe das Hähnchen gegessen und es war sehr lecker. Es hat mir gut geschmeckt.
bullets.note: perfect tense habe gegessen (haben — essen is not a movement verb); war (past of sein); hat ... geschmeckt (impersonal — it tasted good to me)

bullets.prompt: Ask for the bill and say you will come back next year.
bullets.model_answer: Kann ich bitte die Rechnung haben? Nächstes Jahr werde ich wieder kommen.
bullets.note: die Rechnung (bill); können + infinitive at end; future werde + kommen (movement → note: but future tense uses werden, not sein)

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about your eating habits. Include: what you like or dislike eating (using gern / nicht gern), what you eat for breakfast (using zum Frühstück), what you ate yesterday (past tense), and one item you would order in a restaurant (using ich möchte or ich hätte gern).

Mark on: Communication (are all required points covered?), Range of language (gern/lieber/am liebsten after verb, zum + meal, Konjunktiv II möchte/hätte gern, perfect tense habe + eaten), Accuracy (essen stem-vowel change isst, weil + verb at end, noun capitalisation and genders, past participle forms). Be encouraging and formative. gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Gestern habe ich im Restaurant Fisch bestellt, weil er frischer als Fleisch ist. Ich hätte gern ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
gold.correct_text: Gestern habe ich im Restaurant Fisch bestellt, weil er frischer als Fleisch ist. Ich hätte gern ein Glas Wasser, bitte.
gold.translation: Yesterday I ordered fish in the restaurant because it is fresher than meat. I would like a glass of water, please.

gold.question: Complete the sentence — type the missing words (Higher grammar: perfect tense past participles)
gold.english: Yesterday she **cooked** dinner and I **found** it very tasty.
sentence_parts: und ich habe es sehr lecker

gaps.correct_explain: gekocht is the past participle of kochen (to cook): ge- + koch + -t (regular weak verb).

wrong.kocht: kocht is the present tense er/sie form. The past tense needs the past participle: gekocht.
wrong.kochen: kochen is the infinitive. The past tense needs the past participle: gekocht.

gaps.correct_explain: gefunden is the past participle of finden (to find): ge- + fund + -en (strong verb with vowel change i → u).

wrong.gefindet: gefindet is not a real word. Finden is a strong verb — its past participle is gefunden.
